# Indic Tiny TTS frontend fixtures

Reference output of the `indic_tiny_tts` Python package (MIT, Sulabh Katiyar), generated once offline in a network-less sandbox by the build kit script `eval/tts-new-models/indic_frontend_golden.py` from the input corpus `eval/tts-new-models/indic-inputs.json`. Before computing any row, the script checked the SHA-256 of every imported package file against that language's `MANIFEST.json`. Python never runs in Handy; these files are the ground truth of the Rust port in `src/indic/`.

- `hi-frontend.json`: `sulabhkatiyar/indic-tiny-tts-hindi` at `e15ac436560eb24d115d47c0783f62f10a02d30a`, 465 rows `{input, normalized, dropped, chunks, ids}` plus the vocabulary `symbols`.
- `pa-frontend.json`: `sulabhkatiyar/indic-tiny-tts-punjabi` at `40206fc8252d59fd154d90ba0c2f95207ba41a87`, 468 rows of the same shape.
- `en-textnorm.json`: `sulabhkatiyar/indic-tiny-tts-english` at `eea5d4a578c0f18173825a037487cf9c47ed4247`, 311 rows `{input, text_for_chars}` for `textnorm.text_for_chars(input, "en")`.
- `en-frontend.json`: the same English package, 821 rows `{input, normalized, dropped, chunks, ids}` of the full English path (pre-pass `frontend.en_infer.normalize_en`, then `text_for_chars`, the vocabulary filter, chunks and ids) plus the vocabulary `symbols`.
- `en-prepass.json`: the same 821 inputs, rows `{input, tag, pre_pass, single_pass, needs_more_than_one_pass}`: `normalize_en(input)`, one `_one_pass(input)`, and whether the two differ.

- `istft.json`: the package's inverse STFT (`export/onnx_infer.py` `istft`, padding `center`, n_fft 1024, hop 256) on seeded random spectra (seed 20261108), generated by the build kit script `eval/tts-new-models/istft_fixture.py`: the primary 6-frame case at the top level (waveform length 1280) and the 1, 2, 3 and 6-frame cases in `cases`, each with `real`/`imag` as flat row-major `[513][frames]` float32 and the float32 `wav`. The generator also wrote 17 and 40-frame cases; the committed copy drops them (`python3 -I` keeping `cases` with `frames` in 1, 2, 3, 6, then `json.dumps(doc, ensure_ascii=True)` plus a newline).

`dropped` is the set of characters the package's "unsupported characters skipped" warning names. The generator wrote the files with `ensure_ascii=False`; the copies here are the same JSON documents written with `ensure_ascii=True` (`json.dumps(doc, ensure_ascii=True, indent=1)` plus a newline), so they hold no literal non-ASCII characters.

The unit tests `indic::frontend::tests::golden_hindi_matches_reference`, `golden_punjabi_matches_reference` and `golden_english_textnorm_matches_reference` require the Rust port to reproduce every row. `indic::english::tests::golden_english_frontend_matches_reference` and `prepass_and_single_pass_match_reference` do the same for the two English files. `indic::istft::tests::istft_matches_the_numpy_reference` requires the Rust inverse STFT to match every `istft.json` case within 1e-5.

The real-model tests in `indic::engine::real` read the reference waveforms and tensors of the same package (`eval/tts-new-models/indic_reference_audio.py`, ONNX Runtime 1.24.2, one thread) from `HANDY_TTS_INDIC_REFERENCE`; they are not committed.
